correctness.rationale: Proof covers every integer \(k\ge3\), \(n\ge k+1\). Upper bound labels three complementary-edge pairs of \(K_4\), each perfect matching hosting one nonempty color block, so every zero-labeled pair sees each block. Lower bound: if total weight below \(2k\), any globally absent color makes all \(\binom n2\ge2k\) vertices nonempty; otherwise a uniquely supported color forces \(2n-3\) nonempty edges. \(n\ge k+2\) contradiction directly; \(n=k+1\) equality forces all spokes to be singleton-labeled, each other color exactly twice, and a zero pair meeting both bearers defeats rainbow coverage. Finite checker reconstructs adjacency for 78 instances and exhaustively excludes all incidence subsets below 6 for \(n\in\{4,5\}\) and \(k=3\).

value.rationale: Determines an exact natural multicolor domination invariant for every size and arbitrarily large palette k in the two-parameter Kneser family, replacing the naive k-fold labeling of an ordinary 3-vertex dominating set (\(3k\)) by a sharp \(2k\) construction. The exceptional boundary \(n=k+1\) is nontrivial and demands a separate structural lemma. This is not a finite table, parameter relabeling, or routine substitution of existing Kneser k-tuple results.
